Okay, so I need to figure out when Jefferson Davis ended his fight in the Mexican-American War. I remember that Jefferson Davis was the president of the Confederate States of America, but I'm not exactly sure about his role in the Mexican War. Let me try to piece this together.

First, I think the Mexican-American War was from 1846 to 1848. That's when the U.S. and Mexico fought over Texas and some other territories. Jefferson Davis was a military leader back then, right? He was a colonel in the Mississippi Rifles. I believe he fought in the Battle of Buena Vista. I'm not sure about the exact date he left the war, though.

I remember reading somewhere that he was wounded in the leg during the war, which might have led to his resignation or discharge. Maybe that happened around May 30, 1848. But I'm not 100% certain. I should check a reliable source to confirm this date.

Wait, I think Britannica mentions that he ended his service in 1848, but I'm not sure if it's May 30 or another date. I should also look at the Rice University chronology and the Warfare History Network article to see if they have the same information. If they all say May 30, 1848, then that's probably the correct date. If there's any discrepancy, I'll have to note it.

I also recall that after the war, he went on to serve in the U.S. Senate. So, his military service must have ended before that. That gives me a timeframe to check. It makes sense that he would leave the military around 1848 to focus on his political career.

I think the key here is to find a reliable source that explicitly states the end date of his military service in the Mexican War. If multiple sources agree on May 30, 1848, that's the date to go with. If not, I might need to reconsider. But based on what I've found so far, May 30, 1848 seems to be the most consistent date mentioned.
